name: IN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Jim Baird running with large financial edge
Democratic challenger Drew Cox raised only ~$20k
model.rationale: The R+15 district, Baird's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising advantage over a minimally funded challenger leave no evidence pointing toward an upset, and markets agree at roughly 94% Republican. The forecast stays at Safe R with a margin near the district's partisan lean.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Baird or an unexpectedly strong national Democratic environment could narrow the margin, though an upset remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 15 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Jim Baird is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. His challenger, Democrat Drew Cox, has raised only about $20,000 and has minimal cash on hand, giving him little capacity to communicate with voters.

Baird, by contrast, has raised over $350,000 and benefits from more than $500,000 in outside support, though some outside groups have also spent against him. No public polls cover the race and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets put Baird's chances at roughly 94 percent. All available evidence points to a comfortable Republican hold.
